candidate_relations.label: Soft Tissue Infection of right shoulder
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical scenario—profoundly neutropenic patient (ANC 20/μL) with a rapidly progressive, cystic necrotic soft tissue mass in the right shoulder/scapular region, preceded by eczematous plaques (possible cutaneous inoculation site in an agricultural worker), negative galactomannan (arguing against Aspergillus), and failure to respond to antibacterials—strongly points to mucormycosis as the specific etiology. 'Soft tissue infection' is the parent category that encompasses mucormycosis but does not specify the required fungal/Mucorales etiology, making it a partial parent rather than a complete equivalent.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Correctly identifies soft tissue infection at the right shoulder but lacks the specific etiologic diagnosis of mucormycosis (invasive fungal infection by Mucorales); the anatomic localization is consistent but the causative organism is unspecified

case_quality_flags: Agricultural exposure and eczematous plaques at inoculation site are classic clues for cutaneous-to-deep mucormycosis
Negative galactomannan appropriately argues against Aspergillus and supports Mucorales
Cystic necrotic MRI appearance in a profoundly neutropenic host is hallmark of angioinvasive mucormycosis
